plain_english: Now the sixteenth chapter: after scripture-based knowing, reasoned meditation arises; the Lord lists divine qualities beginning with fearlessness.
sanskrit_cite: atha ṣoḍaśo'dhyāyaḥ   etadbuddhvetyuktam | bodhaśca nāma śrutimayajñānānantaraṃ  idamittham-ityevaṃbhūtayukticintābhāvanāmayajñānodayena  vicāravimarśaparāmarśādirūpeṇa  vijātīyanyakkāravirahitatadbhāvanāmayasvabhyastākāravijñānalāb  he sati bhavati | yadvakṣyate-   vimṛśyaivamaśeṣeṇa yathecchasi tathā kuru | (18 a0 | 63 ślo0)   iti | tatra śrutimaye jñāne guruśāstre eva prādhānyena  prabhavataḥ | yukticintābhāvanāmaye tu vimarśakṣamatā  asādhāraṇā śiṣyaguṇasaṃpat pradhānabhūtā | ato'rjunasyāstyevāsau | ityabhiprāyeṇa vakṣyamāṇaṃ  vimṛśyaivam-iti vākyaṃ saviṣayaṃ kartuṃ  parikarabandhayojanābhiprāyeṇāha bhagavānguruḥ-   śrībhagavānuvāca   abhayaṃ sattvasaṃśuddhirjñānayogavyavasthitiḥ | dānaṃ damaśca  yajñaśca svādhyāyastapa ārjavam

plain_english: Non-harm, truth, non-anger, renunciation, non-attachment, non-slander, compassion, non-covetousness, gentleness, modesty, and non-restlessness.
sanskrit_cite: ahiṃsā satyamakrodhastyāga'saktirapaiśunam | dayā  bhūteṣvalaulyaṃ ca mārdavaṃ hrīracāpalam

plain_english: Energy, patience, steadfastness, contentment, non-malice, and absence of excessive pride are the divine wealth of one born divine, Bharata.
sanskrit_cite: tejaḥ kṣamā dhṛtistuṣṭiradroho nātimānitā | bhavanti sampadaṃ  daivīmabhijātasya bhārata

plain_english: Hypocrisy, pride, egoism, anger, harshness, and ignorance are the demonic wealth, Partha.
sanskrit_cite: dambho darpo'bhimānaśca krodhaḥ pāruṣyameva ca | ajñānaṃ  cābhijātasya pārtha sampadamāsurīm

plain_english: Divine wealth liberates, demonic wealth binds; Arjuna is born divine, so he should not grieve.
sanskrit_cite: daivī sampadvimokṣāya nibandhāyāsurī matā | mā śucaḥ sampadaṃ  daivīmabhijāto'si pāṇḍava | āsurabhāgasaṃniviṣṭā tāmasī kilāvidyā | sā pravṛddhayā  divyāṃśagrāhiṇyā vidyayā bādhyate iti vastusvabhāva eṣaḥ | tvaṃ ca vidyātmānaṃ divyamaṃśaṃ sāttvikamabhiprapannaḥ | tasmādāntarīṃ mohalakṣaṇāmavidyāṃ vihāya  vāhyāvidyātmaśatruhananalakṣaṇaṃ śāstrīyavyāpāram  anutiṣṭha-ityadhyāyārambhaḥ | tathāhi | divyāṃśasyemāni  cihnāni tāni sphuṭamevābhilakṣyante damaḥ-indriyajayaḥ | cāpalaṃ-pūrvāparamavimṛśya yatkaraṇaṃ tadabhāvo'cāpalam | tejaḥ-ātmanyutsāhagrahaṇena mitatvāpākaraṇam | daivī  saṃpadeṣā | sā ca tava vimokṣāya-kāmanāparihārāt | atastvaṃ  śokaṃ mā prāpaḥ | yathā-bhrātrādīn hatvā sukhaṃ  kathamaśnuvīya-iti | śiṣṭaṃ spaṣṭam

plain_english: In this world there are two creature-creations, divine and demonic; the divine was spoken in detail, now hear the demonic, Partha.
sanskrit_cite: dvau bhūtasargau loke'smin daiva āsura eva ca | daivo vistarataḥ  prokta āsuraṃ pārtha me śṛṇu

plain_english: This divine wealth is described by abhaya and so on; demonic people do not know activity or cessation, and purity, conduct, and truth are not found in them.
sanskrit_cite: eṣā daivī saṃpaduktā abhayamityādinā | āsurīmāha   pravṛttiṃ ca nivṛttiṃ ca janā na vidurāsurāḥ | na śaucaṃ nāpi  cācāro na satyaṃ teṣu vidyate | pravṛttiḥ-kuta idamutpannamiti | nivṛttiḥ-ka pralīyate iti

plain_english: They call the world untrue, unstable, lordless, and causeless; they see no effect beyond what is seen.
sanskrit_cite: asatyamapratiṣṭhaṃ te jagadāhuranīśvaram | aparasparasambhūtamakiṃcatkamahetukam | na kiṃcit dṛṣṭādanyat kāryaṃ vidyate yatreti-akiṃcitkam

plain_english: Relying on this view, lost selves with small intellects arise as fierce actors, inauspicious for the world's destruction.
sanskrit_cite: etāṃ dṛṣṭimavaṣṭabhya naṣṭātmāno'lpabuddhayaḥ | prabhavantyugrakarmāṇaḥ kṣayāya jagato'śubhāḥ

plain_english: Relying on insatiable desire, filled with pride, conceit, and intoxication, they act cruelly with impure vows.
sanskrit_cite: kāmamāśritya duṣpūraṃ dambhamānamadānvitāḥ | asadgrahāśtāḥ  (-śtiḥ) krūrāḥ pracarantyaśucivratāḥ

plain_english: Relying on immeasurable anxiety until dissolution, making desire-enjoyment supreme, they are certain only this much exists.
sanskrit_cite: cintāmaparimeyāṃ ca pralayāntāmupāśritāḥ | kāmopabhogaparamā  etāvaditi niścitāḥ

plain_english: Bound by hundreds of hope-nooses and devoted to desire and anger, they strive unjustly to gather wealth for desire-enjoyment; their anxiety continues until transmigration and dissolution cease.
sanskrit_cite: āśāpāśaśatairbaddhāḥ kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ | īhante  kāmabhogārthamanyāyenārthasañcayān | cintā teṣāṃ pralayāntā-avirataṃ saṃsṛtipralayāvyuparamāt | etāvaditi-kāmopabhoga eva paraṃ kṛtyaṃ tannāśācca paraṃ  krodhaḥ | ata evāha kāmakrodhaparāyaṇāḥ-iti

plain_english: Today I have gained this; I shall obtain this desire; this is mine and this too; wealth will be mine again.
sanskrit_cite: idamadya mayā labdhamimaṃ prāpsye manoratham | idamastīdamapi me  bhaviṣyati punardhanam

plain_english: That enemy was slain by me; I will slay others too; I am lord, enjoyer, accomplished, strong, and happy.
sanskrit_cite: asau mayā hataḥ śatrurhaniṣye cāparānapi | īśvaro'hamahaṃ  bhogī siddho'haṃ balavān sukhī

plain_english: I am wealthy and of noble birth; who else is equal to me? I will sacrifice, give, and rejoice; thus they are deluded by ignorance.
sanskrit_cite: āḍhyo'bhijanavānasmi ko'nyo'sti sadṛśo mayā | yakṣye dāsyāmi  modiṣye ityajñānavimohitāḥ

plain_english: Many-minded and confused, gone under delusion's control, attached to sense enjoyments, they fall into impure hell; lacking certainty, they fall into hell beginning with avīci, in the continuum of birth and death.
sanskrit_cite: anekacittā vibhrāntā mohasyaiva vaśaṃ gatāḥ | prasaktāḥ  kāmabhogeṣu patanti niraye'śucau | anekacittā iti-niścayābhāvāt | aśucau niraye-avīcyādau  janmamaraṇasantāne ca

plain_english: Self-conceited, stiff, filled with wealth, pride, and intoxication, they sacrifice by name, with hypocrisy and without rule.
sanskrit_cite: ātmasambhāvitāḥ stabdhā dhanamānamadānvitāḥ | yajante  nāmayajñaiste dambhenāvidhapūrvakam

plain_english: Resorting to egoism, strength, pride, desire, and anger, hating the Lord in self and other bodies, they sacrifice by name; such sacrifices do not fruit, and hating worlds they hate the Lord, who is Vasudeva, the all-dwelling.
sanskrit_cite: ahaṅkāraṃ balaṃ darpaṃ kāmaṃ krodhaṃ ca saṃśritāḥ | māmātmaparadeheṣu pradviṣanto'bhyasūyakāḥ | yajñairyajante nāma-niṣphalamityarthaḥ | krodhena hi sarvaṃ  naśyatītyarthaḥ | yadvā | nāmayajñaiḥ-saṃjñāmātreṇaiva ye  yajñāstaiḥ | athavā | nāmārthaṃ-prasiddhyarthaṃ ye yajñāḥ  yena yajñayājyayam-iti vyapadeśo jāyate | te dambhapūrvakā eva  natu phalanti | krodhādirūṣitatvādeva lokāndviṣanto māmeva  dviṣanti | ahaṃ vāsudevo hi sarvāvāsaḥ

plain_english: I continually cast those hateful cruel lowest men into asuri wombs.
sanskrit_cite: tānahaṃ dviṣataḥ krūrānsaṃsāreṣu narādhamān | kṣipāmyajasramaśubhāsvāsurīṣveva yoniṣu

plain_english: Born in asuri wombs, deluded ones fail to reach me and go to the lowest state; hating ones act harmfully and cause hell-fall, so I cast them into asuri wombs.
sanskrit_cite: āsurīṃ yonimāpannā mūḍhā janmani janmani | māmaprāpyaiva  kaunteya tato yāntyadhamāṃ gatim | ātmani ca dveṣavantaḥ ātmano hyahitaṃ nirayapātahetumācaranti | tāṃścāhaṃ āsurīṣveva yoniṣu kṣipāmi

plain_english: Desire, anger, and greed are the threefold gate of hell and destruction of self; therefore one should abandon this triad.
sanskrit_cite: trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ | kāmaḥ  krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet | yataḥ kāmādikaṃ trayaṃ narakasyaiva dvāram tasmādetattyajet

plain_english: Freed from these three dark gates, O Kaunteya, a man practices for self and then goes to the supreme destination.
sanskrit_cite: etairviyuktaḥ kaunteya tamodvāraistribhirnaraḥ | ācaratyātmanaḥ  śreyastato yāti parāṃ gatim

plain_english: This is not a human saying to disregard; scripture here is beginningless authority. One who abandons scriptural rule and acts from desire attains neither perfection, happiness, nor supreme destination.
sanskrit_cite: na caitat puruṣavacanamityanādaraṇīyam apitu anādi śāstramatra  pramāṇam-ityucyate   yaḥ śāstravidhimutsṛjya vartate kāmakārataḥ | na sa  siddhimavāpnoti na sukhaṃ na parāṃ gatim

plain_english: Therefore scripture is authority for you in determining action and inaction; having known this, you should do scripturally prescribed action here. Abandoning scriptural rule and deliberating by one's own opinion leads to fall into hell, so do not determine action and inaction by self-intellect; this is the purport.
sanskrit_cite: tasmācchāstraṃ pramāṇaṃ te kāryākāryavyavasthitau | jñātvā  śāstravidhānoktaṃ karma kartumihārhasi | śāstravidhiṃ tyajataḥ svamanīṣayaiva kāryākāryavicāraṃ  kurvataḥ pratyuta narakapātaḥ | tasmādātmabuddhyā  kāryākāryavyavasthāṃ mā kārṣīriti tātparyam

plain_english: In ignorance, one should not determine duty by one's own intellect; rather, by the rule declared in scripture, and scripture itself increases knowing. Thus ends the sixteenth chapter of Abhinavagupta's Gathering of the Gita's Meaning.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   abodhe svātmabuddhyaiva kāryaṃ naiva vicārayet | kintu  śāstroktavidhinā śāstraṃ bodhavivardhanam | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe ṣoḍaśo'dhyāyaḥ
